deploy: The deploy pipeline runs three stages: build, sign, and canary rollout.
Builds are cached by lockfile hash and reuse the previous image layer.
Signing happens after the canary passes its first health probe.
The deploy key is owned by the platform team and rotates every 90 days.
Rollback is automatic when the canary error rate passes two percent.
Canary traffic starts at five percent and doubles every ten minutes.
All rollout events are appended to the deploy audit log in object storage.
billing: Invoices are generated on the first business day of each month in UTC.
The billing retry job runs every six hours for up to five attempts.
Failed retries escalate to the finance alias after the third attempt.
Tax is computed per line item using the customer's registered country.
Credits are applied before tax and never after an invoice is finalized.
Every invoice change writes an immutable event to the billing ledger.
Refunds require two approvals and settle within seven business days.
auth: The auth service issues JSON Web Tokens signed with an Ed25519 key pair.
Access tokens expire after fifteen minutes and are never renewed in place.
Refresh tokens last thirty days and are revoked on password change.
Signing keys are rotated every ninety days by the security team.
Session records live in Redis with a sliding expiry of one hour.
Every failed login increments a per-account counter that resets hourly.
Service-to-service calls use mutual TLS instead of bearer tokens.
search: The search index rebuilds every night at 02:00 UTC from the primary database.
Documents are embedded with the same model used by the query path.
Results are re-ranked by a cross encoder limited to fifty candidates.
The re-ranker runs on two GPUs and adds about forty milliseconds per query.
Synonym expansion is applied before embedding, not after retrieval.
Queries slower than five hundred milliseconds are logged with their parameters.
Index snapshots are retained for fourteen days for rollback.
mobile: The mobile app ships a bundled model that runs entirely on device.
Sync uses a delta protocol that sends only changed fields.
The offline queue is capped at two hundred pending mutations.
Conflicts resolve last-write-wins with a server timestamp tiebreak.
Crash reports are uploaded over Wi-Fi only by default.
The bundle identifier is com.example.mobile and releases are signed with an enterprise certificate.
Version gates block clients older than two major releases.
pipeline: The data pipeline ingests events through Kafka with twelve partitions.
Each consumer commits offsets only after the sink acknowledges the batch.
Late arriving events are accepted for up to seventy-two hours.
Deduplication keys on the event id and the producer's sequence number.
The warehouse load runs hourly and writes to the analytics schema.
Schema changes require a migration reviewed by the data team.
Backfills are rate limited to ten thousand rows per second.
support: Support tickets are triaged within one business hour by an on-call rotation.
Priority one incidents page the on-call engineer immediately.
Macros are versioned and audited before they can be sent to customers.
The escalation policy names Dana Ruiz as primary contact for enterprise accounts.
Satisfaction surveys are sent twenty-four hours after a ticket closes.
Every ticket export expires after thirty days inside the shared bucket.
Chat transcripts are retained for twelve months and then deleted.
infra: Production runs in three availability zones behind a global load balancer.
Each zone holds one database replica and two application nodes.
Terraform state lives in an encrypted bucket with versioning enabled.
Node images are rebuilt weekly and pinned by digest.
Alerts route to PagerDuty and page after two consecutive failures.
Disk usage above eighty percent triggers an automatic expansion.
The backup window is 01:00 to 03:00 UTC with 35-day retention.
